abstract: Several proteins involved in dopaminergic neurotransmission have been implicated in Parkinson's disease (PD), including synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2C (SV2C). At least seven SNPs in SV2C are associated with PD, including variants that modify: PD risk, PD risk in GBA carriers, PD severity, contribution of environmental factors (e.g., nicotine) to PD, and PD patient response to L-DOPA and dopamine therapies. Although the specific function of SV2C remains unknown, there is significant evidence supporting a role of SV2C in mediating vesicular dopamine content, vesicular trafficking, and neurotransmitter release. Furthermore, SV2C directly associates with -synuclein and mediates the content of neurotoxicants within synaptic vesicles. Taken together, these data suggest that SV2C plays a critical role in mediating PD risk and pathogenesis. To investigate whether SV2C mediates PD outcomes, transgenic Caenorhabditis elegans (C. elegans) expressing human SV2C, human -synuclein, or both, were exposed to the PD-associated neurotoxicants 1-methyl-4-phenylpyridinium (MPP+), rotenone, and paraquat, and evaluated for PD outcomes including lethality and dopamine-mediated motor behavior. Although SV2C-expressing C. elegans showed a shorter lifespan at baseline, SV2C expression conferred organism-level protection against MPP+ and paraquat-induced lethality. While -synuclein expression exacerbated lethality following MPP+ and paraquat exposure, SV2C provided partial rescue of lethality in -synuclein-expressing C. elegans. However, no differences in lethality were observed based on genotype following rotenone exposure. Interestingly, sublethal toxicant exposure did not reveal a protective effect of SV2C expression on motor behavior for any of the toxicants. To determine whether SV2C's modulation of vesicular uptake mediated the protection against lethality from PD-associated neurotoxicants observed in C. elegans, in vitro assays of vesicular dopamine uptake dynamics were performed. SV2C expression resulted in a protective shift in toxicant-induced uptake inhibition following MPP+ and rotenone exposure; however, there was no paraquat-induced inhibition of vesicular uptake observed in vitro. Taken together, these data suggest that while SV2C plays a protective role in mediating organism-level survival in C. elegans following MPP+ and paraquat exposure, the mechanisms of protection and the role of SV2C in modulating vesicular dopamine dynamics and dopamine-mediated behaviors following toxicant exposure require further analysis. Future studies can evaluate additional PD outcomes in these exposure models and investigate SV2C-mediated mechanisms of protection such as regulation of neurotransmitter handling and oxidative stress.
